locations.note: The Soviet campaign recreates combat in Stalingrad and makes Order 227 part of the battle.
Churkin and Isakovich fall back to the fortified village of Mtsensk on the road to Moscow and hold it against German armour.
Embedded as a war correspondent, Isakovich follows the Red Army's assault to liberate Orsha.
The Red Army storms Lublin and uncovers the Majdanek concentration camp outside the city.
Sent to a penal battalion, Isakovich witnesses the storming of the Poznań citadel.
The penal battalion fights in the destruction of the encircled German Ninth Army at Halbe.
The final campaign battle takes the Soviet forces into Berlin in 1945.
In a Siberian gulag in 1952, Colonel Churkin interrogates Isakovich about his war journal and finally lets him escape with it.

routes.name: Lt. Lev Isakovich
routes.note: Isakovich's journal opens at Stalingrad, goes back to the 1941 defence of Mtsensk, returns to Stalingrad and then follows the Red Army through Orsha, Lublin, Poznań and Halbe to Berlin.
